- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is trending up, cap the rise at 1–2% above recent mean to avoid false momentum.  
- After a strong price spike (forecast > 10% above recent 7-day high), apply a 3–5 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until price stabilizes.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.8) and forecast is erratic, use a 3-day moving average to smooth out noise before projecting.  
- If forecast mean is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 30-day horizon, apply a 5–10% downward bias correction for the next 7-day window.  
- For sentiment history with repeated low values (≤0.2) and forecast showing recovery, delay the upward correction by 2–3 days to avoid premature rebound.
